programme: NCOA4-driven ferritinophagy: NCOA4 acts as the selective autophagy receptor that delivers ferritin to the autophagosome/lysosome, releasing chelatable iron and generating the free-iron pool that feeds either iron-dependent lipid peroxidation (ferroptosis) or iron-hungry proliferative metabolism, depending on the cell's state.
role_in_a: In ischemic/reperfused brain tissue, NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy releases iron that drives ferroptotic death of neurons and endothelium; the retrieved papers place this at the level of specific regulators of NCOA4 abundance (KLF6/NSUN2 m5C modification enhancing ferroptosis in OGD/R neurons) and at the level of intervention (exosome therapy reducing ferroptosis, electroacupuncture acting on the same ferritinophagy/ferroptosis mechanism, review evidence tying ferritinophagy to autophagy control in stroke).
role_in_b: In thymoma, a single retrieved paper reports that PRRC2A-mediated m6A modification of NCOA4 promotes proliferation of thymic epithelial tumor cells, consistent with the iron-addiction phenotype common to proliferating tumors rather than with cell death.
shared_axis: Both settings converge on NCOA4 as the rate-limiting node for iron release from ferritin, with RNA-modification enzymes (m5C/NSUN2 in stroke, m6A/PRRC2A in thymoma) independently tuning its abundance; the same ferritinophagy machinery is pushed toward lethal iron overload in ischemic neural tissue and toward growth-supporting iron turnover in a proliferating epithelial tumor.
reasoning: NCOA4-ferritinophagy is a real, nameable mechanism with solid, disease-specific placement in Stroke (five papers, mechanistic and interventional) but only one, very recent paper placing it in Thymoma, and no retrieved source discusses the two diseases together despite two hits being tagged as 'concerns both' - their text is stroke-specific. The cross-disease link therefore rests on reasoning about shared iron/ferroptosis biology, not on anything retrieved, and stroke and thymoma have no obvious anatomical or clinical connection.
support: PMID 41478321 - NSUN2/KLF6 m5C modification of NCOA4 enhances ferroptosis in OGD/R-injured neurons, tying NCOA4 dosage to stroke injury; PMID 42603839 - endothelial progenitor exosomes reduce ferroptosis and promote neovascularization after stroke, in a ferritinophagy-relevant context; PMID 40189641 - electroacupuncture study framed around ferroptosis mechanisms (incl. ferritinophagy) in ischemic stroke; PMID 40706815 - review of neuronal autophagy regulation in stroke covering ferritinophagy, text is stroke-specific despite being tagged 'both diseases'; PMID 38834843 - review establishing ferritinophagy/ferroptosis as an operative mechanism in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury; PMID 42420246 - PRRC2A-mediated m6A modification of NCOA4 promotes thymic epithelial tumor proliferation, the sole direct placement of NCOA4 in Thymoma.
how_to_falsify: Silence or block NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy (NCOA4 knockdown, or disruption of the NCOA4-ferritin interaction) in (1) an OGD/reperfusion stroke model and check whether ferroptotic death and the labile iron pool actually fall, and (2) a PRRC2A/m6A-status-matched thymic epithelial tumor line and check whether proliferation and iron flux fall. If NCOA4 loss changes neither phenotype through a ferritinophagy-dependent mechanism - e.g. if thymoma proliferation instead depends on NCOA4's separate role as an androgen-receptor coactivator (its own inferred targets are AR, KLK3, TFF1, not iron-handling genes) - the shared-axis account fails.
caveats: Tissue pairing (blood vs thymus) is anatomically distant and the 30 patient-group comparisons come from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the 20/30 concordance for NCOA4 reflects sub-group replication within few underlying cohorts, not 30 independent confirmations. NCOA4's own recurrence (20/30) is mid-tier, not the strongest in the list. Exclusion of tissue-generic factors (GFI1, HLX, ETS2, CIITA, FOXO1, ID2, BCL6, MEF2C, EZH2, ZBTB4, TBX21, SPIB) and single-view factors (SRCAP, CIITA, FOXO1, HTATIP2, PPARG, ID2, BCL6, GFI1, MSX1) shows the remaining signal is not simply generic immune/blood-thymus overlap or a one-cohort artifact. RBPJ scored higher (27/30) with three direct Stroke papers and a target signature (FOXP3, CD40, RBPJL) suggestive of thymic Notch biology, but no retrieved evidence places it in Thymoma, so it was left out of this account rather than used to force a stronger story. NCOA4's own network-inferred targets (AR, KLK3, TFF1) reflect its separate androgen-receptor-coactivator identity, not the ferritinophagy function the cited papers describe - a real tension in the record that any wet-lab follow-up should resolve first.
